({{US$|1.27 billion}}) (2017) | owner = [[Vedanta Resources]] | num_employees = 10,000 (2012) | parent = | divisions = | subsidiaries = | footnotes = | founded = {{start date and age|1979}} | hq_location_city = [[Mumbai]], [[Maharashtra]] | hq_location_country = India | hq_location = | num_locations = | caption = | defunct = 2021; 4 years ago | website = {{url|https://videoconindustriesltd.com/}} }} '''Videocon Industries Limited''' was an Indian multinational [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]], headquartered in [[Mumbai]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.videoconindustriesltd.com/ |title=Videocon Industries Investor Relations: Corporate Governance |access-date=4 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180605195013/http://videoconindustriesltd.com/ |archive-date=5 June 2018 |url-status=live }} The company was founded in 1979, by [[Venugopal Dhoot]]. The group had 17 manufacturing sites in [[India]] and plants in [[mainland China]], [[Poland]], [[Italy]] and [[Mexico]]. It was the third largest [[picture tube]] manufacturer in the world{{cite web|url=http://forbes.com/global/2007/0108/030.html|title=Tube Opportunist|work=Forbes.com|access-date=31 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191231093607/https://www.forbes.com/global/2007/01/08/030.html|archive-date=31 December 2019|url-status=live}} valued at {{USD}}5.5 billion.{{Cite news|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/1150830/jsp/business/story_39749.jsp|title=Videocon unit takes off|date=2015-08-30|access-date=2017-05-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180709064558/https://www.telegraphindia.com/1150830/jsp/business/story_39749.jsp|archive-date=9 July 2018|url-status=dead}} The company stopped trading and entered corporate insolvency proceeding in June 2018. In June 2021, [[NCLT]] approved [[Vedanta Resources|Vedanta Group]]'s bid to take over Videocon, paving the way for the new ownership.{{Cite web|date=2021-06-09|title=Vedanta arm gets nod for Videocon takeover|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/business/companies/vedanta-arm-gets-nod-for-videocon-takeover-7350074/|access-date=2021-12-16|website=The Indian Express|language=en}} == Early years == In 1985, [[Aurangabad]] based Nandlal Madhavlal Dhoot founded and incorporated Videocon International with a goal of manufacturing 1 [[lakh]] TV sets per year. "''Videocon became the first company to bring colour TVs in India''," claims Anirudh Dhoot, the founder's grandson ([[Venugopal Dhoot|Venugopal Dhoot's]] son) and Videocon's current director.{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/independence-day-special-how-videocon-changed-the-countrys-viewing-experience-with-colour-tvs/articleshow/48436464.cms|title=Independence Day Special: How Videocon changed the country's viewing experience with colour TVs|last=Bhatt|first=Shephali|date=2015-08-12|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2020-01-26}} ==Corporate profile== The Videocon group's core areas of business are [[consumer electronics]] and [[home appliance]]s. They diversified into areas such as [[Direct-broadcast satellite|DTH]], [[Electrical power industry|power]] and [[oil exploration]]. ===Consumer electronics=== In India, the group sold consumer products like [[Color television|colour televisions]], [[washing machine]]s, [[air conditioners]], [[refrigerator]]s, [[microwave oven]]s and many other home appliances, through a multi-brand strategy with the largest sales and service network in India. Since the entry of Korean Chaebols and their rising popularity in the Indian market, Videocon from a stand-point of market leader has seen a slow decline to become a no. 3 player in India. The company continued to do well in the washing machine and refrigerator segment.{{cite news|last=Singh|first=A|title=Market share|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-08-03/news/33020190_1_anil-arora-lg-india-indian-durables|access-date=31 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131103040801/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-08-03/news/33020190_1_anil-arora-lg-india-indian-durables|archive-date=3 November 2013|url-status=dead}} ===Mobile phones=== In November 2009, Videocon launched its new line of mobile phones.{{cite web |url=http://www.videoconmobiles.com |title=Videocon Mobile Phones, Compare/Buy Online Mobile Phones Deals India |publisher=Videoconmobiles.com |access-date=29 July 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230143514/http://www.videoconmobiles.com/ |archive-date=30 December 2014 |url-status=usurped }} Videocon has since launched a number of handsets ranging from basic colour FM phones to high-end Android devices. In February 2011, Videocon Mobile Phones launched the hitherto unknown concept of 'Zero' paise (1 [[paisa]] is the 100th unit of 1 [[Indian rupee]]) per second with bundled [[Subscriber Identity Module|SIM]] cards of Videocon mobile services for 7 of its handset models. extract:
Videocon Industries Limited was an Indian multinational conglomerate, headquartered in Mumbai. The company was founded in 1979, by Venugopal Dhoot. The group had 17 manufacturing sites in India and plants in mainland China, Poland, Italy and Mexico. It was the third largest picture tube manufacturer in the world valued at US$5.5 billion.
The company stopped trading and entered corporate insolvency proceeding in June 2018. In June 2021, NCLT approved Vedanta Group's bid to take over Videocon, paving the way for the new ownership.
